The median nerve innervates all muscles in the superficial layer of the anterior arm except flexor carpi ulnaris. This includes flexors of the wrist (minus ulnar), flexors of the digits, pronator teres and flexor digitorum profundus. Therefore, since the patient cannot flex the PINKY or RING fingers, the median nerve has been damaged. The ulnar nerve innervates the intrinsic muscles of the hand, flexor carpi ulnaris and some of the wrist flexors. The radial nerve innervates the posterior compartment of the arm and extensors of the forearm, as well as the lateral interosseous muscle and the thenar muscles. The musculocutaneous nerve innervates the anterior compartment of the arm and the extensor muscles of the forearm. The axillary nerve innervates the deltoid.  Nerve injury can result in either neurapraxia or axonotmesis. In neurapraxia, there is loss of axonal conduction but the endoneurium and perineurium remain intact - there is no clinical evidence of injury to the nerve. There is a good prognosis with full recovery within weeks/months. In axonotmesis there is a severing of the axon with associated Wallerian degeneration. There is variable prognosis depending on whether there is also damage to the endoneurium and perineurium.  Source: 'Nerves' lecture from Case 15.
